detail.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity
detail.summary: Chemical memory based on autocatalytic networks relies on compositional persistence (hysteresis) rather than template-directed information transfer. Thermodynamic frameworks suggest that selection requires distinct separation between functional coding and the metabolic persistence of the network.
detail.reason: Synthesis of thermodynamic foundations with non-equilibrium systems research.

detail.title: Chemical Memory to Heredity Transition
detail.question: What experimental evidence distinguishes autocatalytic chemical memory from template-directed heritable information transfer in non-equilibrium systems?
detail.reason: Aligning research effort with the required chemical_heredity focus and investigating the fundamental transition in prebiotic evolution.

detail.title: Foundations of Chemical Heredity
detail.question: How do non-equilibrium systems transition from simple persistence to stable, heritable information storage?
detail.reason: Notebook updated; advancing to search for concrete thresholds.

children.title: Compositional Heredity and Thermodynamic Persistence in Prebiotic Networks

detail.title: Compositional Heredity and Thermodynamic Persistence in Prebiotic Networks
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes findings on how non-templated autocatalytic networks achieve stable heritable compositional states. It clarifies that such heredity can emerge from growth-division cycles in multistable reaction networks rather than relying exclusively on template replication.
detail.reason: Updating notebook findings based on new evidence regarding composition operations and protocell division models.

detail.title: Compositional Heredity in Autocatalytic Networks
detail.question: Can multistable autocatalytic reaction networks maintain stable heritable compositional states across diverse growth-division regimes to sustain evolution by natural selection?
detail.reason: Notebook revised with new evidence; keeping project active to explore further thermodynamic constraints.

detail.title: Compositional Heredity across Growth-Division Regimes
detail.summary: Updated analysis of whether multistable autocatalytic reaction networks can maintain heritable compositional states across growth-division regimes using newly incorporated evidence.
detail.reason: Incorporating newly collected peer evidence to update the findings on compositional heredity and thermodynamic selection.
